title: Common-stage natural point transport with normalized semilinear return
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its fixed algebraic closure $k$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $Y_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Write $g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ for geometric Frobenius. For each finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, use the rationalized constructible categories and derived pullbacks in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Let $\mathcal C_Y=D^b_c(Y,\Omega)$ be the literal category of pairs $(E,K)$ and common-stage morphism classes of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. All composition and scalar comparisons are the specified rationalizations of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], including equality of scheme morphisms, units and finite iterations. 
Fix $n\geq1$ and $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, with induced geometric point $\bar x:s\to Y$; thus $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$. Put $P_E=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}L\bar x_E^*$, using the rational point-fibre functor in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and $T_E=Lg_{Y,E}^*$. For $K\in D^b_c(Y,E)$ define
$$J_{E,K}:P_EK\longrightarrow P_ET_E^nK$$
as the $n$ successive point transports on $L\bar x_E^*K$, followed by the return comparison for $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$, exactly as the first two factors of the local operator in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. No Weil structure on $K$ is required. For every underlying morphism $u:K\to L$,
$$P_E(T_E^nu)J_{E,K}=J_{E,L}P_E(u).$$
For $E\subset M$ let $b_K:P_EK\otimes_E M\xrightarrow{\sim}P_M(K\otimes_E M)$ be the canonical point comparison and $d_{n,K}:(T_E^nK)\otimes_E M\xrightarrow{\sim}T_M^n(K\otimes_E M)$ the iterated pullback scalar comparison, both with the specified normalization. Then
$$P_M(d_{n,K})b_{T_E^nK}(J_{E,K}\otimes_E M)=J_{M,K\otimes_E M}b_K.$$
The $b_K$ are natural in all underlying morphisms; this equation respects identity extensions and towers $E\subset M\subset N$. With these comparisons, the finite-stage point-complex functors $P_E$ define a functor $P$ from $\mathcal C_Y$ to the common-stage category $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Omega)$ of bounded finite-dimensional point complexes (formed by the same pair and Hom-colimit construction). The maps $J_{E,K}$ define morphisms $J_K:P(K)\to P(T^nK)$ in that category, independent of finite-stage representatives and compatible with their further scalar extensions. For every common-stage underlying morphism $u:K\to L$,
$$P(T^nu)J_K=J_LP(u).$$
This uses the semilinear return equality displayed above, without assuming $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar x$. It applies to all bounded constructible complexes, without a Weil-stable integral lattice or a finite-Tor-amplitude condition on integral reductions.

proof.text: Write $S_{M/E}=-\otimes_E M$ on scheme complexes and $R_{M/E}=-\otimes_E M$ on point complexes. Let $a_{E,M,K}:S_{M/E}L\bar x_E^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}L\bar x_M^*S_{M/E}K$ be the specified pullback comparison and let $\beta_{E,M,N}:R_{M/E}\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}N\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}S_{M/E}N$ be the inverse rational sections comparison. Then $b_{E,M,K}=\operatorname{Fib}_{s,M}(a_{E,M,K})\beta_{E,M,L\bar x_E^*K}$. The naturality of both factors gives naturality of $b$ for every rational underlying morphism. The identity and tower equations for the two factors give those for $b$: in the tower composite move $\beta$ past $a$ by naturality, then replace the two successive $a$'s and the two successive $\beta$'s by their direct comparisons. These are exactly the rationalizations specified in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] and [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], using the rational point functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization] with $X_0=Y_0$, $m=n$, $y=x$ and $\Lambda=E$. Its map $t_{y,m,K}$ is precisely $J_{E,K}$: both use the successive point transports and the return $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$ with the specified comparisons, as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Its naturality is $P_E(T_E^nu)J_{E,K}=J_{E,L}P_E(u)$. Its final displayed equation is exactly the asserted scalar equation, with the $b$ of step 1 and the stated $d_n$. It also gives the identity and tower compatibility with these very comparisons. The hypotheses are separated finite type $Y_0$, the rationalized constructible category, and $n\ge1$; no Weil structure on $K$ is among them. Its explicit no-finite-Tor clause applies here.

proof.text:
For objects set $P(E,K)=(E,P_EK)$. For a representative $u:K_M\to L_M$, where $K_M=S_{M/E}K$ and $L_M=S_{M/F}L$, set
$$A_M(u)=b_{F,M,L}^{-1}P_M(u)b_{E,M,K}.$$
Use the source equivalence relation of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and the target one of [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. For $M\subset N$, substitute the tower formula for each $b_{E,N}$ and use naturality $P_N(S_{N/M}u)b_{M,N,K_M}=b_{M,N,L_M}R_{N/M}(P_Mu)$. Cancellation gives $A_N(u_N)=(A_M(u))_N$, with the displayed source and target associators. Hence representatives equal over a further common field have equal images. Identities map to identities. Over one common field, $A_M(v)A_M(u)=b_H^{-1}P_M(v)b_Lb_L^{-1}P_M(u)b_K=A_M(vu)$, so the classes define the required functor. Step 1 supplies naturality and tower equations used in this substitution.

proof.text:
Put $D_{E,M,K}=P_M(d_{n,K})b_{E,M,T_E^nK}$. By the common-stage pullback action of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the functor $PT^n$ acts on $[M,u]$ by
$$B_M(u)=D_{F,M,L}^{-1}P_M(T_M^nu)D_{E,M,K}.$$
Step 2 says $D_{E,M,K}R_{M/E}(J_{E,K})=J_{M,K_M}b_{E,M,K}$. Substitute it and finite-stage naturality into the preceding formula:
$$B_M(u)R_{M/E}(J_{E,K})=D_{F,M,L}^{-1}P_M(T_M^nu)J_{M,K_M}b_{E,M,K}$$
$$=D_{F,M,L}^{-1}J_{M,L_M}P_M(u)b_{E,M,K}=R_{M/F}(J_{F,L})A_M(u).$$
Thus naturality holds over the very field representing $u$, for arbitrary underlying $u$, by cancellation of the specified invertible $D$'s. The normalized $d_n$ and their tower equations are those of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]; the scalar and finite-stage naturality equations used here are those of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization].

proof.text: Define $J_{(E,K)}$ to be the class represented at $E$ by $J_{E,K}$, with the unit identifications. At any larger field $M$, its representative is $R_{M/E}(J_{E,K})$; step 2 identifies this with $D_{E,M,K}^{-1}J_{M,K_M}b_{E,M,K}$. Therefore the stage-$M$ construction gives the same class under the canonical transition isomorphisms. Scalar extension of the equation in step 4, followed by the tower identifications, gives that equation for $u_N$ at every $N\supset M$. If two representatives agree at $N$, both sides agree there, hence define the same equation in the target Hom colimit [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category]. This proves $P(T^nu)J_K=J_LP(u)$ for every common-stage morphism. In particular every common-stage isomorphism intertwines these components; finite-stage models remain literal pairs, identified by their canonical comparison isomorphisms. All steps use only the semilinear return of step 2, never $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar x$.
